items.sentence: The theory that spoken words account for only about seven percent of communication involving emotions *may surprise* many people.
items.pattern: S with Noun clause (that...) + Vt + O

items.sentence: This *was first proposed* by Dr. Albert Mehrabian, a famous psychology professor.
items.pattern: S + Passive verb phrase + Prepositional phrase + Appositive phrase

items.sentence: According to his studies, we *achieve* about 55% of our emotional communication with our bodies, for they typically demonstrate our true feelings and what we're actually thinking.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase + S + Vt + O + for + S + Vt + O + Noun clause (what...)

items.sentence: Therefore, understanding people's body language *is* an important ability to help us better interpret others' messages.
items.pattern: Gerund phrase (S) + Vl + C + Infinitival phrase

items.sentence: Being able to read body language well *is* helpful in determining whether or not someone is telling the truth.
items.pattern: Gerund phrase (S) + Vl + C + Gerund phrase + Noun clause (whether...)

items.sentence: When people are lying, there *are* usually three telltale signs: making stiff body movements, touching or scratching themselves, and making eye movements.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (When...) + There + Vi + S + Gerund phrases

items.sentence: Typically, liars *exhibit* fewer arm and hand gestures.
items.pattern: Adverb + S + Vt + O

items.sentence: When they do make such gestures, their movements *are* usually stiff, and their hands *tend* to stay close to the body rather than move in an outward direction.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (When...) + S + Vl + C + and + S + Vi + Infinitival phrase

items.sentence: Moreover, liars often *can't help* but touch or scratch their faces, their necks, or behind their ears.
items.pattern: S + Modal verb phrase + Coordinated bare infinitives + O

items.sentence: They sometimes *rub* their eyes without being conscious of it as well.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: Whether people are telling falsehoods or not *can also be detected* by observing how their eyes move as they speak.
items.pattern: Noun clause (Whether...) as S + Passive verb phrase + Gerund phrase + Noun clause (how...) + Adverbial clause (as...)

items.sentence: When right-handed people say true things, their eyes *move* to their left.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (When...) + S + Vi + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: In contrast, when they are lying or being "creative" with the truth, their eyes *tend* to drift toward their right.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (when...) + S + Vi + Infinitival phrase

items.sentence: The reverse *is* true for left-handed people.
items.pattern: S + Vl + C + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: Another significant type of telling body language *is connected* to love.
items.pattern: S + Passive verb phrase + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: In the case of romantic feelings, people's bodies subconsciously *provide* an indication for someone to whom they are attracted.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase + S + Vt + O + Relative clause (to whom...)

items.sentence: Under the circumstances, their eyes *do* most of the "talking."
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase + S + Vt + O

items.sentence: Initially, they may *glance* at a person from a distance and for just slightly longer than normal.
items.pattern: Adverb + S + Vi + Prepositional phrases

items.sentence: Afterward, they may *look* away and finally *rest* their eyes on him or her again for an even longer period.
items.pattern: Adverb + S + Vi / Vt (Compound predicate) + O + Prepositional phrases

items.sentence: Furthermore, they automatically *track* or *repeat* his or her actions without even knowing it.
items.pattern: S + Vt (Compound predicate) + O + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: If he or she sits back, they will *follow suit*.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (If...) + S + Vi (Phrasal verb)

items.sentence: If that person takes a sip of water, they will probably *do* the same.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (If...) + S + Vt + O

items.sentence: Aside from copying behavior, they often *can't help* pointing their feet and shoulders toward the one they adore or standing closer to the object of their affection than to others.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase + S + Modal verb phrase + Gerund phrases + Relative clause

items.sentence: All of the previously mentioned points *reveal* the idea that one of the best methods for interpreting people's thoughts and emotions is to pay attention to their body language.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O + Noun clause (that...) + Infinitival phrase

items.sentence: By understanding the signals that people send out with their body language, we may *interact* in a more meaningful way with our fellow human beings.
items.pattern: Gerund phrase with Relative clause (that...) + S + Vi + Prepositional phrases

items.sentence: Best of all, we can *do* it without even saying a single word!
items.pattern: Adverbial phrase + S + Vt + O + Prepositional phrase

text_genre.raw_text:
Passage Structure Analysis
Introduction (Para 1): Introduces Dr. Mehrabian’s theory ($55\%$ of emotional communication is body language) and states the thesis (reading body language helps interpret true feelings).
Body 1: Detecting Deception (Para 2): Identifies three body language signs of lying—stiff gestures, touching/scratching the face/neck, and specific eye movement patterns.
Body 2: Indicating Attraction (Para 3): Explains non-verbal signs of romantic interest—prolonged eye contact, subconscious mirroring of actions, and pointing feet/shoulders toward the person.
Conclusion (Para 4): Summarizes body language as a key tool for understanding hidden thoughts and fostering meaningful non-verbal communication.
